issues.legal_issue: A trespasser whose possession has become settled may defend that possession against forcible dispossession, even by the true owner.
material_facts: A complainant had encroached on part of a public road, cultivated the land, and grown a paddy crop there.
The complainant had been in peaceful possession for two to three weeks before the incident, and the appellants knew of that possession.
The appellants entered the cultivated field with their cattle and tried to pass through it, damaging the crop; a complaint about the encroachment was already pending before the Panchayat.
issues.conclusion: The complainant had settled possession and was entitled to defend it. The appellants could not forcibly dispossess him and had to pursue remedies under the law.
issues.legal_principle: Under the principle applied in Puran Singh & Ors. v. State of Punjab, settled possession sufficient to support a right of private defence requires effective, actual possession over a sufficient period, known to the owner or not concealed, with the process of dispossession complete; cultivation and a grown crop are relevant indicia. A true owner may remove a trespasser while the trespass is still in progress, but must use legal remedies once the trespasser has accomplished possession to the owner's knowledge.

rule.if: criminal_appeal and trespasser_in_actual_possession and possession_known_to_owner and possession_accomplished and crop_grown

predicates.criminal_appeal: The case is an appeal in a criminal proceeding.
predicates.trespasser_in_actual_possession: A trespasser was in actual physical possession of the disputed property.
predicates.possession_known_to_owner: The owner knew, or the possession was not concealed from the owner, that the trespasser possessed the property.
predicates.possession_accomplished: The trespasser had completed the process of taking possession rather than merely beginning to trespass.
predicates.crop_grown: The trespasser had cultivated the land and grown a crop on it.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal concerns a trespasser who has accomplished actual possession known to the owner and has grown a crop, the trespasser may defend that settled possession.

issues.legal_issue: A person who initiates an assault against a person in settled possession cannot claim a right of private defence of person or property against that person.
material_facts: The complainant was in peaceful, settled possession of the cultivated land, and the appellants knew of that possession.
The appellants entered the field with their cattle, damaged the crop, and opened the assault after the complainant's party protested.
The courts below found that the appellants were the aggressors.
issues.conclusion: The appellants, as aggressors, could not claim a right of private defence of person or property.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the private-defence principles discussed in Puran Singh & Ors. v. State of Punjab: a person in settled possession may defend that possession, and a person who is the aggressor cannot rely on private defence against the party defending its possession. The Court also relied on the rule that an owner must use legal remedies to remove a trespasser whose possession is already accomplished.

rule.if: criminal_appeal and complainant_in_settled_possession and accused_initiated_assault and accused_attempted_forcible_entry

predicates.criminal_appeal: The case is an appeal in a criminal proceeding.
predicates.complainant_in_settled_possession: The complainant was in settled possession of the disputed property.
predicates.accused_initiated_assault: The accused opened the assault on the complainant's party.
predicates.accused_attempted_forcible_entry: The accused entered or tried to pass through the complainant's possessed land by force.

issues.definition: When accused persons in a criminal appeal attack a complainant who is in settled possession after attempting forcible entry, they cannot claim private defence.

issues.legal_issue: Injuries to accused persons do not by themselves discredit the prosecution when the prosecution evidence sufficiently explains them as occurring during a mutual fight.
material_facts: Three accused persons sustained injuries during the occurrence.
Prosecution witnesses said that members of the complainant's party wielded weapons when the accused attacked them, acting in self-defence.
The deceased and several prosecution witnesses also sustained injuries, and the evidence showed that a mutual fight occurred.
issues.conclusion: The prosecution had sufficiently explained the accused persons' injuries, so the case could not be rejected on the ground that those injuries were unexplained.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the evidence as a whole and held that the injuries to the accused did not undermine the prosecution where the witnesses explained that they occurred in the course of the mutual fight and the prosecution side also suffered injuries. No earlier case or statutory provision was relied on for this determination.

rule.if: criminal_appeal and accused_sustained_injuries and prosecution_witnesses_explained_injuries and prosecution_side_also_injured

predicates.criminal_appeal: The case is an appeal in a criminal proceeding.
predicates.accused_sustained_injuries: One or more accused persons sustained injuries in the occurrence.
predicates.prosecution_witnesses_explained_injuries: Prosecution witnesses explained that the accused persons' injuries occurred during the fight after the accused attacked.
predicates.prosecution_side_also_injured: The deceased or members of the prosecution party also sustained injuries in the occurrence.

issues.definition: When evidence in a criminal appeal explains the accused persons' injuries during a fight and the prosecution side was also injured, the objection based on those injuries does not defeat the prosecution case.

issues.legal_issue: A medical opinion that an injury required a particular movement of the weapon does not create a reasonable doubt when the eyewitness account is consistent with the injury and the weapon could have caused it.
material_facts: Eyewitnesses consistently testified that the deceased was assaulted in the abdomen with a pointed weapon.
The medical evidence showed an abdominal injury that could have been caused by that weapon, although the doctor said the injury could have required the weapon to be rotated after it was thrust.
The incident involved a mutual fight, making it difficult for witnesses to observe the exact manner in which the weapon was used.
issues.conclusion: The medical evidence did not contradict the eyewitness account so as to put the prosecution case out of court.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the precise manner of infliction need not have been observed in a mutual fight where the eyewitness account establishes the assault and the medical evidence confirms that the weapon could have caused the injury. No earlier case or statutory provision was relied on for this determination.

rule.if: criminal_appeal and eyewitnesses_consistently_described_assault and medical_evidence_compatible_with_weapon and exact_weapon_movement_unobserved

predicates.criminal_appeal: The case is an appeal in a criminal proceeding.
predicates.eyewitnesses_consistently_described_assa: The eyewitnesses gave consistent evidence that the deceased was assaulted with the identified weapon.
predicates.medical_evidence_compatible_with_weapon: The medical evidence showed an injury that could have been caused by the weapon described by the eyewitnesses.
predicates.exact_weapon_movement_unobserved: The witnesses could not observe the exact movement of the weapon during the fight.

issues.definition: When eyewitness evidence consistently describes an assault and medical evidence confirms the weapon could have caused the injury, an unobserved detail of the weapon's movement does not create reasonable doubt.

issues.legal_issue: An accused who inflicts an injury sufficient to cause death and has no right of private defence is liable for murder.
material_facts: One appellant inflicted the fatal abdominal injury on the deceased with a pointed weapon.
The injury was sufficient to cause death.
The appellant had no right of private defence because the complainant was in settled possession and the appellants were the aggressors.
issues.conclusion: The conviction of the appellant who inflicted the fatal injury under section 302 of the Indian Penal Code was affirmed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, reasoning that once the right of private defence was unavailable and the injury inflicted was sufficient to cause death, the assailant could not escape conviction for murder.

rule.if: criminal_appeal and accused_inflicted_fatal_injury and injury_sufficient_to_cause_death and no_right_of_private_defence

predicates.criminal_appeal: The case is an appeal in a criminal proceeding.
predicates.accused_inflicted_fatal_injury: The accused inflicted the injury that caused the victim's death.
predicates.injury_sufficient_to_cause_death: The injury inflicted by the accused was sufficient to cause death.
predicates.no_right_of_private_defence: The accused had no right of private defence in the circumstances.

issues.definition: When an accused in a criminal appeal inflicted an injury sufficient to cause death and had no right of private defence, the murder conviction is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: Common intention to cause grievous hurt cannot be attributed to other participants when the fatal or grievous assault was an individual act and the others were acting to assert a bona fide claim of right.
material_facts: The fatal assault was an individual act of one appellant.
The other appellants had joined in an effort to assert a supposed or bona fide claim to use the public road.
The Court found no common intention among those other appellants to cause death or grievous injury.
issues.conclusion: The convictions and sentences of the other appellants under sections 326/34 of the Indian Penal Code were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the common-intention principle under section 34 with section 326 of the Indian Penal Code, finding that a shared purpose to assert a supposed or bona fide claim of right did not establish common intention to cause grievous hurt when the grievous assault was an individual act.

rule.if: criminal_appeal and grievous_assault_was_individual_act and others_shared_claim_of_right and no_common_intention_to_cause_grievous_hurt

predicates.criminal_appeal: The case is an appeal in a criminal proceeding.
predicates.grievous_assault_was_individual_act: The act causing death or grievous injury was committed by one participant individually.
predicates.others_shared_claim_of_right: The other participants acted to assert a supposed or bona fide claim of right.
predicates.no_common_intention_to_cause_grievous_hu: The evidence did not establish a common intention among the other participants to cause grievous hurt.

issues.definition: When an individual commits the grievous assault and the other participants share only a claim of right without common intention to cause grievous hurt, their grievous-hurt common-intention conviction is set aside.

issues.legal_issue: Participants who jointly attack others and cause simple injuries with a shared intention to cause hurt may retain convictions for common-intention hurt and trespass.
material_facts: The appellants made a concerted attack on several prosecution witnesses using a pointed weapon or sticks.
The evidence accepted by the courts below established that the attacks caused simple injuries to those witnesses.
The appellants entered land in the complainant's settled possession.
issues.conclusion: The convictions and sentences under sections 324/34, 323/34, and 447 of the Indian Penal Code were left undisturbed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied sections 324/34 and 323/34 of the Indian Penal Code to the concerted attacks, finding a common intention to cause simple hurt, and section 447 to the established criminal trespass. It distinguished that shared intention from an intention to cause death or grievous hurt.

rule.if: criminal_appeal and concerted_attack_with_weapons and simple_injuries_caused and common_intention_to_cause_simple_hurt and accused_entered_anothers_possession

predicates.criminal_appeal: The case is an appeal in a criminal proceeding.

predicates.simple_injuries_caused: The attack caused injuries classified as simple hurt.
predicates.common_intention_to_cause_simple_hurt: The participants shared an intention to cause simple hurt.
